children.note: Adds a node one level down and starts typing right away.

children.text: Move: drag a node onto another one

children.note: Collapsed branches show a number: that many nodes are hidden inside. Click the number to expand again.
The most important keys. You hardly ever need the mouse.
The **outline** is ideal for quick notes in a lecture. The **map** shows how things connect. Both always show the same content.
Right-click › *Shape*. Tip: one shape per kind of node – you can tell from afar what a node is.
Background, border, font size, **bold**/*italic* and text color apply to this node only. Copy a style: select a node in the map, ⌘C. Apply it: select another (even a new) node, ⌘R.

children.text: Branch color applies to all child nodes

children.note: Sidebar › *Layout*: also direction, spacing and branches (curved or angled, tapered).
Drag and drop **next to** a node. Dropping **onto** a node attaches it there. Back to its place: right-click › *Reset Position*.
Sidebar › *Theme*: adjust the colors, then *Save as Own Theme …* – it is then available for all documents and can be exported as a file.
children.text: Save and share your own theme

children.note: Or right-click a node or the empty area of the map.
children.text: Style: in the toolbar; theme and layout in the sidebar (⇧⌘I)

children.note: That keeps the map clear – and while learning you first see only the keywords. This makes you **recall** the details instead of just recognizing them.
children.text: Keyword in the node, explanation in the note
Open a note: click the page icon

children.note: Task, tags, note, link/image/formula and style appear in the toolbar as soon as a node is selected. The sidebar shows themes and layout.

children.note: Before office hours: *View › Highlight › Unclear* – and you see all open questions at once.
Fades out everything without the tag. Before the exam: highlight only **Exam** and review exactly these nodes.
Tags mark **what role** a node plays in learning. Set them via *Node › Tags* or ⌥⌘1 to ⌥⌘7.

children.text: Check off: click the box or ⇧⌘D

children.note: The circle shows the progress of all tasks below: empty = open, half = partly done, full = done.
The library collects the open tasks from **all** documents – your study plan for the week. Double-click opens the mind map at the right spot.

**Node › Sync Tasks with Reminders** creates a list for this mind map in Apple's Reminders.

You can then check off tasks in both apps – on your iPhone too. New reminders in the list become tasks in the map. Syncing happens while the mind map is open.
Main branches = chapters or guiding questions. At most about **7 branches** per level – more is hard to remember. Clockwise order = learning order.

This is **retrieval practice**: collapse a branch, say out loud what is in it, then check. It works much better than reading again.

In the German learning examples the **Selbsttest** branch is collapsed. The answers are in the notes.
Spaced repetition. Add tasks for it to your study plan.
Searches nodes and notes. ⌘G jumps to the next match.
PDF for printing, Markdown or OPML for other apps.
Shrunk to one page or spread legibly over several A4 pages – just as the map looks on screen.
Finds your mind maps even by a word that appears only in a node or a note.

In the Shortcuts app under “MindMaps”: New Mind Map, Add Node, Find Mind Maps, Open Mind Map and Export Mind Map.

Example: “Export Mind Map” (format PDF, nothing selected = last used) followed by “Save File”.

Or right-click › *Connect to …* and then click the target node.
Move the curve with the handle in the middle; double-click it to change the label.
children.text: Cross-connection: drag a node onto another with ⌥

children.note: Everything except the selected branch fades – good for reviewing a single chapter.
Full screen, then → branch by branch. **N** shows the notes, **Esc** ends.
Web addresses or links to nodes in other mind maps (right-click › *Copy Link to This Node*, then paste into the other node).
From the Finder or the Photos app. Resize it with the handle at the bottom right of the image or in the sidebar.
LaTeX notation: **^** superscript, **_** subscript, **\frac{a}{b}** fraction, **\sqrt{x}** root, **\alpha** Greek letters, **\cdot** multiplication dot.

root.note:
**Welcome!** This mind map is an example itself. Read it branch by branch – start at the top right, then go clockwise.

**Basic rule:** A node holds just a keyword. Everything you want to explain belongs in the **note** (the small page icon on the node).

Try anything you like here. The file is yours – delete, change, check off.
